findings.title: Frontier dual-air witness 50036056 is reproduced by the original under a race-relative stimulus-equivalence test: a one-frame simultaneous hop
source_artifacts: signed census research/qa-cumulative-ledger frontier_exact_coverage tokens 79968377c3bf214b60c95a12 (2580) and fb53e5eaddfbcae645a046f6 (3420)
findings.observation: Original frames 2577-2579 (native-equivalent 2579-2581): P2 air 1 -> 2 -> 0, P1 air 0 -> 1 -> 0, y_speed 19/38 for one frame. The original's normalized fingerprint equals the native census token at both 2580 and 3420.
findings.uncertainty: Quantized census fields only; $0545/$0547 semantics remain provisional; the frontier binary's entry lag is inferred (RF-003), not directly measured.
findings.resolving_experiment: None needed for parity. Optional: original writer trace of $0545/$0547 at original 2577-2579 to name the hop mechanism.
findings.consequence: Not a discrepancy. Removes the only frontier dual-air lead from the QA-01 queue; the 120-frame sampler caught a one-frame coincidence, not sustained flight.
findings.resolution: Under race-relative stimulus equivalence (post-entry original input shifted -2) the original matches the native row (local candidate evidence, native 4c1c8b56... not the frontier 28501fa3...). The identical-input-byte executed observation of runs 38509912672/38520105599, which differs at host 2580, stands as executed. No event acceptance (USA 0/45).

findings.title: Two protocols: identical absolute-host input (executed, differs at host 2580) versus race-relative stimulus equivalence (matches); same-host comparison alone cannot separate entry phase from behaviour
source_artifacts: .github/workflows/two-player-reference.yml step 'QA-01 paired source dual-air seed 50036056' (run 38509912672, artifact qa01-dual-air-paired-50036056)
findings.observation: Run 38509912672 recorded raw_both_air_at_2580 = {original: false, native: true} and QA-01 classified it as a provisional state divergence. A local unshifted original replay reproduces the hosted original column byte for byte (2579 00/01, 2580 00/02, 2581 00/00). The race-relative original (lag 2) reproduces the native column exactly.
findings.uncertainty: None for the dual-air reading; the hazard applies to any same-absolute-host paired replay on a route whose engines enter at different host frames.
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-01: keep run 38509912672 (and 38520105599) as executed identical-input observations and record the race-relative result beside them; run any further writer trace race-relatively as well.
findings.consequence: Prevents a false original/native dual-air discrepancy from entering the QA-01 queue.

findings.title: Modern native enters the ordinary 2P race 2 host frames after Snes9x and Beetle-bsnes (1136 vs 1134)
source_artifacts: calibration: the seed-independent 1740 token matches at L=0 and L=2 only
exploration set: first 10 cases of run 38506108109 agree at 2580 and 3420 for L=2 (10/10), L=0 (9/10), L=1 (0/10)
findings.observation: Measured directly on a current-main Modern candidate (4c1c8b56..., source fda6ace) in 36 paired cases: first inRace=1/race_tick=1 at native 1136, Snes9x 1134; the pinned Beetle-bsnes build also enters at 1134 (the older staircase figure 1133 does not hold for it). Consistent with the census cross-check's independent L=2 selection.
findings.uncertainty: Measured on the current-main candidate, not on the 28501fa3 frontier binary itself; that binary's L=2 is implied by population fingerprint agreement.
findings.consequence: Any original/native replay of frontier input must shift post-entry input by -2 and compare native F with original F-2.
findings.resolution: Entry lag 2 measured per case by tools/qa_frontier_original_crosscheck.py paired (measured_entry_host).

findings.title: Original-emulator cross-check of the frontier census population
findings.observation: All 10,400 cases of the five signed frontier runs replayed on the original (Snes9x, L=2): 10,378 coarse agreement, 22 census-attribution-ambiguous (the original's token is owned by an earlier case, consistent with the ~21 cross-shard repeats documented in the 10k postmortem), 0 coarse divergence. Where the native run used the 15-frame observer, feature incidence is identical. Original 15-frame both-air incidence over the 10k population is 31/10,000.
findings.uncertainty: Quantized fields (x//64, y//32, v//64, rotation//16) can hide sub-bin differences; agreement is not strict equality.
findings.resolving_experiment: None for this route; exact paired comparison (26/26) confirms the quantized result.
findings.consequence: Converts 10,400 native-only cases into original/native comparisons without a single new native process.
findings.resolution: No original/native divergence on the frontier route at quantized census precision; candidate evidence (local) until independently re-executed.

findings.title: $121B/$121D 'offscreen' predicate is never nonzero; bank-82 split-screen sentinels are the source-qualified culling signal
source_artifacts: ordinary 2P regression asserts screen1 P2 (0x70,0x70) and screen2 P1 (0x30,0x30) at $1501-$150E on both runtimes
findings.uncertainty: Native sentinel incidence is not in the census; given exact semantic-WRAM agreement on this route (RF-004) it is expected to be identical.
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-08: if a culling question needs it, ask for per-frame sentinel transitions (a 100-case observer validation), not case incidence; otherwise no work.
findings.consequence: Stops further volume aimed at a dead register; gives QA-08 a named, source-qualified observer.
findings.observation: Original-side measurement over 400 cases: both bank-82 opponent-offscreen sentinels appear at some sampled frame in 400 of 400 cases (racers separate within the race). Case incidence is therefore uninformative; a per-frame or per-transition (on-screen to off-screen) count is the discriminating form.

findings.title: 2P raw 7E:009F (wTextPos) 0x84 phase lasts one frame longer on native than on Snes9x and Beetle-bsnes (48 of 49 seeds +1, 1 seed +2)

reproducer.command: python3 tools/qa_frontier_original_crosscheck.py paired --native-exe <Modern candidate> --seed 50036056 --arm rotation --lag 2 --finish-hold 4000 --frames 1128-1140,1620-4800/60,4801-6400 --snesref ... --core <snes9x|beetle> --ledger <ledger.json> --work W --out R

findings.observation: 49 seeds, measured lag 2 in all: decoded source fields identical through laps-zero (same frame in 49/49) and until the reference's 0x16 restoration; result-menu onset on the same frame in 43, one frame earlier on native in 6; scheduler parity at onset does not predict the outcome. Raw semantic WRAM ($0200+) first differs 1-2 native frames BEFORE result-menu (0x84) onset in 49 of 49 seeds (all five arms). For 50036056 at native 5196-5198 the original builds the 10-byte list at 7E:2000 in one frame (first word 01->02->04); native shows a different intermediate one frame later (01->03->04). 7E:0BDE/0BFE start at 0xCC->0xC8 on the original but 0xC4->0xC0 on native, an offset of 8 held through the whole phase. The 0x84 phase then lasts 34 frames on Snes9x (and on Beetle-bsnes for 50036056) and 35 on native in 48 of 49 (36 for 50024003). Per-core boundaries differ: Snes9x onset same frame in 43 and native one earlier in 6, with the restore later on native; Beetle-bsnes (50036056) onset native 5198 vs 5199, both restore 5233. 7E:009F is the DrawText cursor wTextPos (#1543), so 0x84->0x16 is a raw terminal signature.
findings.uncertainty: Local candidate evidence (current-main native 4c1c8b56...) until independently re-executed with raw-dump receipts. 83:987D Sram_RestoreDirectPage is a downstream 207-word SRAM->DP copy, not a proven diverging decision. Gameplay significance pending the upstream caller and actual 7E:009F writer on each core. Semantics of 7E:2000 (update list?) and 7E:0BDE/0BFE (unnamed in the repo) are unknown; whether the 8-unit offset is guest-visible (sprite Y or banner position) or only scheduling is unproven.
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-01: instrument the upstream result-onset/restore caller and the actual 7E:009F writer on both reference cores and native (per-core axes kept separate); see RF-014 for the common lag-frame lead.
findings.consequence: A cheap deterministic 2P reproducer of the same result-handoff seam behind the open 1P Switcher +4704/+4702 strict divergence; it does not change any comparator or acceptance.

findings.title: Native race-entry lag is phase-dependent (2 or 3 frames) when the 2P menu route is delayed

reproducer.command: shift every event of tests/input/two-player-first-race.input by +k (k=0..7), dump 1120+k..1149+k on Snes9x and the Modern native, take first inRace=1

findings.observation: Lag native minus Snes9x = 2,2,3,2,3,2,2,2 for k = 0..7. The original absorbs a k-frame delay one for one; native quantizes it, as if a vblank/fade-gated wait sometimes costs one extra frame.
findings.uncertainty: Local candidate evidence until independently re-executed with raw receipts. Mechanism unproven; staircase notes point at the 80:FAC9 / $4212 vblank-sensitive fade for entry. Whether the same mechanism lengthens the 0x84 result phase (RF-012) is a hypothesis.
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-01: compare native and original iteration counts of the entry fade wait loop for k=1 (lag 2) and k=2 (lag 3); if the extra frame is the wait loop, test the same loop in the 0x84 phase.
findings.consequence: Race-relative comparisons must measure lag per case on any route other than the fixed stock prefix; gives RF-012 a cheap, input-only mechanism discriminator.

findings.title: Native completes fewer game frames than the original at screen loads; every load's black screen is 1-3 frames longer than on the high-accuracy bsnes core (player-visible)

reproducer.command: stock tests/input/two-player-first-race.input on Snes9x and the Modern native, dump every 4 host frames 2..1126, count decrements of 7E:00C6 (one per 80:FAC9 vblank-wait pass via 80:FADF)

source_artifacts: reference/imported/reverse-engineering/nitrodon/bank 80.txt 80:FAC9-80:FAF9 (LDA $4212 BMI/BPL wait; DEC $C6 mod 32; STA $0BDE/$0BFE from table 80:FBAF)
generic setup_project native (fda6ace framework pin), same census: 772 game frames
bsnes-libretro high-accuracy core (tools/toolchain.json pin 05439f96) agrees with Snes9x on every blank-screen run
findings.observation: Over host frames 2-1126: native 773 FAC9 passes, Snes9x 801, Beetle-bsnes 802 (two independent reference cores agree within one frame). Both engines run one pass per host frame in steady menus. Native loses passes only in transition/slide windows (menus 0x84, 0xD7, 0x3D, 0x6D, 0x91; e.g. host 442-446: native 0, original 4). The resulting 7E:00C6 offset of 4 (mod 32) is frozen during the race and explains RF-012's 7E:0BDE/0BFE offset of 8 exactly (0BDE = table[C6>>1]). A generic SNESRecomp native built by setup_project without the Modern product patches completes 772 game frames, so the deficit is in the shared framework/generated-code timing, not the Modern host. One-frame localisation of the 0x84->0xD7 transition: all engines hold 7E:00C6 at 0x02 from host 426 (a load); Snes9x resumes decrementing at 437 and Beetle at 436, native at 442; menu 0xD7 appears at 440 on both reference cores and at 446 on native. The no-input attract cycle (host 2-4002, one counter-rewrite window excluded) shows the same deficit: native 1311 passes, Snes9x 1326, Beetle-bsnes 1327. Player-visible confirmation (tools/qa_blank_screen_census.py, every frame, framebuffers only): on the stock 2P route the reference (bsnes-libretro high-accuracy = Snes9x; Beetle within one frame) shows black-screen runs 248-276, 401-443, 988-1150; native shows 248-278, 404-449, 988-1151 (+2, +3, +1). Attract cycle: +2, +3, +3, +2 with later loads starting 17 frames late by host 3632. 2P race-finish transition (seed 50036056): +1. Generic SNESRecomp build: +2, +3, 0. In the first load (reference 248-276) WRAM at $0200+ stays byte-identical between native and Snes9x while VRAM fills: the reference writes 738 words per frame by CPU (unrolled STA $2118 at 81:CD70-81:D09C, nitrodon bank 81), native's VRAM progress falls 1 then 2 frames behind and converges at 278, so native completes the same CPU-bound decompress-to-VRAM work in about 7% more host frames. The second load (reference 401) starts later on native because the transition waits for the 7E:00C6 phase, which native reaches 4 frames later.
findings.uncertainty: Local candidate evidence until independently re-executed with raw receipts. Neither reference core is cycle-exact hardware, but they agree with each other and disagree with native by 28-29 frames. The source of native's deficit (host frame pacing, DMA/HDMA cost modelling or the $4212 model) is unknown; AGENTS forbids tuning $4212 merely to match one emulator. First suspect, unverified: the framework's synthetic $4212 beam model (snesrecomp pinned in tools/toolchain.json at cd5875cbdaf1 runner/src/snes/snes.c readReg 0x4212: fixed 64-clock advance per poll in static-recomp mode; docs/VIRTUAL_HW_CONTRACT.md), which sets how many host frames a polled load costs; upstream notes a sibling case (SMRPG boot fades at the wrong frame count).
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-01 / native-fidelity: compare native and reference CPU cycles per iteration of the bank-81 VRAM writer (81:CD70-81:D09C) in the host 248-278 load (e.g. native master_cycles per frame against bsnes's 1364x262 budget); the frame-count gap there is ~7% (31 vs 29). AGENTS forbids tuning $4212 merely to match one emulator.
findings.consequence: A single cheap observer (7E:00C6) measures game-frame vs host-frame divergence anywhere in the game; likely common cause of RF-012 and RF-013, and of the 1P result-handoff phase seam.
